tooltip.appliedcooking:kitchen_station.d: Station node that connects to Applied Energistics 2 grids
jei.appliedcooking.kitchen_station.1: The ME Kitchen Station lets your Cooking for Blockheads cooking table craft with items (and fluids like water and milk) straight from your Applied Energistics 2 network.
jei.appliedcooking.kitchen_station.2: To link it, open an ME Wireless Access Point on your powered network, drop the station into its wireless-terminal slot, and take it back out. The link is saved on the block and works even across dimensions, as long as the Access Point stays chunk-loaded.
jei.appliedcooking.kitchen_station.3: Place the linked station in your kitchen, next to the cooking table or wired in through counters. Its screen glows purple when connected, and it draws a little power from the network while running.
appliedcooking.guide.landing: Welcome!$(br2)$(2)Applied Cooking$() connects your $(6)Cooking for Blockheads$() kitchen with $(5)Applied Energistics 2$(), letting you cook straight from your ME network inventory.
category.appliedcooking.name: Applied Cooking
category.appliedcooking.description: A mod that allows you to use items from your $(5)Applied Energistics 2$() network inventory directly in your $(6)Cooking for Blockheads$() kitchen multi-block!$(br2)One new block is added to Minecraft.
entry.appliedcooking.kitchenstation.name: ME Kitchen Station
entry.appliedcooking.kitchenstation.intr: The $(l)ME Kitchen Station$() is the one block you need to bridge $(6)Cooking for Blockheads$() with $(5)Applied Energistics 2$().$(br2)Placed in your kitchen, it hands your whole $(5)ME network$() inventory to the Cooking Table, so every stored item becomes an ingredient. It even pulls $(o)fluids$() like water and milk from network storage.$(br2)Craft it, link it, and drop it into your kitchen. Here's how.
entry.appliedcooking.kitchenstation.craf: Craft the $(l)ME Kitchen Station$() as shown.$(br2)Straight out of the grid it isn't tied to anything yet. The next step links it to your $(5)AE2$() network so it knows where to pull from.
entry.appliedcooking.kitchenstation.link: You link the Station at an $(5)ME Wireless Access Point$(), the same block that serves wireless terminals.$(br2)$(l)Right-click$() a powered Access Point to open it, drop the Station into its wireless-terminal slot, and it comes back $(2)linked$(); take it out again.$(br2)The link is saved on the block itself, so the Station keeps reaching the network from any distance, even another dimension.
entry.appliedcooking.kitchenstation.plac: An example kitchen layout. Tap the eye to preview it in the world.
entry.appliedcooking.kitchenstation.stat: The Station's screen shows its status at a glance.$(br2)$(5)Purple$() means it's $(2)linked and powered$(): the Cooking Table can cook with everything in your $(5)ME network$(), water and milk included, for a little power.$(br2)$(c)Red$() means it's $(o)linked but the network is out of reach$(). It has an Access Point saved but can't talk to it, so check the network has power to spare and that the Access Point's chunk stays loaded.$(br2)$(8)Dark$() means it isn't $(o)linked$() yet. Open a Wireless Access Point on a powered network and drop the Station into its terminal slot to link it.
